title: Monday's close: a huge bounce
text: Stocks had one of their best days in years. The S&P 500 fund SPY rose 4.7% and the Nasdaq 100 fund QQQ rose 7.0%, after Friday's big drop. NVIDIA led the way, up 31% in one day, after its board brought back Jensen Huang as CEO. A big bounce feels great, but it does not mean the bumpy ride is over. Wednesday has a normal session, markets are closed Thursday for Thanksgiving, and Friday closes early at 1 pm.

title: NVIDIA jumps 31% as its CEO returns
text: NVIDIA closed at $165.05, up from $125.53. The board voted to reinstate Jensen Huang, who left on November 12. The company's own review of what happened is still going on, so more news could come. The stock is still about 32% below its high of the past year. Its risk score dipped from 6.7 to 6.4, which moves it from High to Medium.

title: Chip makers bounced too
text: Other companies that build parts for AI rose with NVIDIA. TSMC, which makes chips for NVIDIA and others, gained 13.9%. Vertiv, which cools and powers data centers, gained 12.1%. AMD rose 6.9% and Broadcom 3.0%. The big AI users moved less: Alphabet and Meta rose about 6.5%, Amazon 3.5% and Microsoft 1.6%. That shows the suppliers usually swing harder in both directions.

title: A December rate hike still looks likely
text: The Federal Reserve decides on interest rates on December 9. Traders still see a better than 90% chance of a quarter point hike. The 2 year Treasury yield, which follows Fed expectations closely, rose on Monday. Higher rates make borrowing more expensive, which can slow down fast growing companies.

title: Lesson 63: Why the best days often follow the worst days
text: Friday was one of the worst days of the year. Monday was one of the best. That happens a lot: the biggest up days often come right after the biggest down days, while people are still scared. If you sell in a panic, you can miss the bounce. Studies of the S&P 500 show that missing just a handful of the best days over many years can cut your total return a lot. That is why many long term investors say time in the market beats timing the market. Staying invested is hard when it feels scary, so having a plan before the storm helps.

title: What this update covers
text: Prices, 52 week ranges and beta for all 17 names come from FMP at Monday's close. Analyst price targets and company numbers like P/E are for NVDA, TSM, AMD, GOOGL, AMZN, MSFT, META, LMT and GE. The 10 year Treasury yield is a monthly average from Alpha Vantage, through October. News comes from company filings and news reports. This is for learning, not advice to buy or sell.
